claims.text: What the image looks like MV thickening, hockey-stick deformity, MV area ≤1.5 cm² → mitral stenosis (most often rheumatic)
claims.quote: MV thickening, hockey-stick deformity, MV area ≤1.5 cm² Mitral stenosis (most often rheumatic)

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Valves: morphology, regurgitant jets (color Doppler), gradient/area (CW Doppler)
claims.quote: Valves - morphology, regurg jets (color Doppler), gradient/area (CW Doppler).

claims.text: Confirmed by echo: 2D typically shows abnormal valve and subvalvular structures, calcification, the degree of stenosis and LA size; Doppler gives the transvalvular gradient and pulmonary artery pressure; the normal mitral orifice is 4 to 5 cm2
claims.quote: Diagnosis of mitral stenosis is suspected clinically and confirmed by echocardiography. Typically, 2-dimensional echocardiography shows abnormal valve and subvalvular structures. It also provides information about the degree of valvular calcification and stenosis and LA size. Doppler echocardiography provides information about the transvalvular gradient and pulmonary artery pressure. The normal area of the mitral valve orifice is 4 to 5 cm2.

claims.text: Moderate: valve area > 1.5 to 2.5 cm2 or pressure half-time < 150 msec; severe: valve area ≤ 1.5 cm2 or pressure half-time ≥ 150 msec, with symptoms often present
claims.quote: Severity of mitral stenosis is characterized echocardiographically as (1): Moderate: Valve area > 1.5 to 2.5 cm2 or diastolic pressure half-time < 150 msec Severe: Valve area ≤ 1.5 cm2 or diastolic pressure half-time ≥ 150 msec; symptoms are often present

claims.text: TEE can detect or exclude small LA thrombi, especially in the LA appendage, which usually cannot be seen transthoracically
claims.quote: Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) can be used to detect or exclude small LA thrombi, especially those in the LA appendage, which usually cannot be seen transthoracically.

claims.text: CXR usually shows straightening of the left heart border (dilated LA appendage) and widening of the carina; a double shadow of an enlarged LA may be seen along the right heart border; Kerley B lines indicate interstitial edema from high LA pressure
claims.quote: Chest radiograph usually shows straightening of the left cardiac border due to a dilated LA appendage, and widening of the carina. With barium in the esophagus, the lateral chest radiograph will show the dilated LA displacing the esophagus posteriorly. The main pulmonary artery (trunk) may be prominent; the descending right pulmonary artery diameter is ≥ 16 mm if pulmonary hypertension is significant. The upper lobe pulmonary veins may be dilated. A double shadow of an enlarged LA may be seen along the right cardiac border. Horizontal lines in the lower posterior lung fields (Kerley B lines) indicate interstitial edema associated with high LA pressure.

claims.text: Causes Usually rheumatic fever; calcific degeneration is increasingly seen in older patients
claims.quote: Mitral stenosis is usually caused by rheumatic fever, although calcific degeneration is increasingly observed in older patients.

claims.text: Leaflets become thickened and immobile; the orifice narrows from fusion of the commissures and shortened, thickened, matted chordae
claims.quote: In mitral stenosis, mitral valve leaflets become thickened and immobile and the mitral orifice becomes narrowed due to fusion of the commissures and the presence of shortened, thickened, and matted chordae tendineae.

claims.text: LA size and pressure rise; pulmonary venous and capillary pressures rise and may cause pulmonary hypertension and RV failure; LA enlargement predisposes to atrial fibrillation, a risk factor for thromboembolism
claims.quote: Left atrial (LA) size and pressure increase progressively to compensate for mitral stenosis; pulmonary venous and capillary pressures also increase and may cause secondary pulmonary hypertension, leading to right ventricular (RV) heart failure, tricuspid regurgitation, and pulmonary regurgitation. Rate of progression varies. LA enlargement predisposes to atrial fibrillation, a risk factor for thromboembolism.

claims.text: Symptoms Initial symptoms are usually those of heart failure (exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, PND, fatigue); many patients are asymptomatic until they become pregnant or develop atrial fibrillation
claims.quote: Many patients are asymptomatic until they become pregnant or atrial fibrillation develops. Initial symptoms are usually those of heart failure (eg, exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, fatigue).

claims.text: Loud first heart sound and an early diastolic opening snap, then a low-pitched decrescendo-crescendo rumbling diastolic murmur, best at the apex at end-expiration in the left lateral decubitus position
claims.quote: Heart sounds include a loud first heart sound and an early diastolic opening snap followed by a low-pitched decrescendo-crescendo rumbling diastolic murmur, heard best at the apex at end-expiration when the patient is in the left lateral decubitus position; the murmur increases after a Valsalva maneuver, exercise, squatting, and isometric handgrip.

claims.text: With atrial fibrillation and no anticoagulation, up to approximately 5% annual stroke risk; occasionally the first sign is an embolic event such as stroke
claims.quote: In patients with atrial fibrillation and mitral stenosis who are not taking anticoagulants, there is up to an approximately 5% annual risk of stroke; occasionally the initial symptoms and signs of mitral stenosis are those of an embolic event such as stroke (2).

claims.text: Less common: hemoptysis (rupture of small pulmonary vessels). Hoarseness from compression of the left recurrent laryngeal nerve by a dilated LA or pulmonary artery is called Ortner syndrome
claims.quote: Less common symptoms include hemoptysis due to rupture of small pulmonary vessels and pulmonary edema, particularly during pregnancy when blood volume increases. Hoarseness due to compression of the left recurrent laryngeal nerve by a dilated LA or pulmonary artery is called Ortner syndrome.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: anticoagulate if AF; balloon valvuloplasty
Mildly symptomatic patients usually respond to diuretics and, with sinus tachycardia or AF, to beta-blockers or calcium channel blockers for rate control
claims.quote: Mildly symptomatic patients usually respond to diuretics and, if sinus tachycardia or atrial fibrillation is present, to beta-blockers or calcium channel blockers for rate control.

claims.text: A vitamin K antagonist (eg, warfarin) prevents thromboembolism with current or past AF, embolism or LA thrombus; non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants are not indicated in rheumatic mitral stenosis
claims.quote: Anticoagulation with vitamin K antagonists (eg, warfarin) is indicated to prevent thromboembolism if patients have or have had atrial fibrillation, embolism, or a left atrial thrombus. Extended restoration of sinus rhythm is rarely possible. Anticoagulation may also be considered in the presence of dense spontaneous contrast or an enlarged left atrium (M-mode diameter > 50 mm) because these findings are associated with thromboembolism, although anticoagulation for these patients has not been studied. All patients should be encouraged to continue at least low levels of physical exercise despite exertional dyspnea. Note that non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants are not indicated for anticoagulation in patients with rheumatic mitral stenosis.

claims.text: Severe MS: intervention is indicated with any symptoms if the valve suits percutaneous balloon commissurotomy (may be considered when asymptomatic with pulmonary pressure > 50 mm Hg or new-onset AF)
claims.quote: Intervention is indicated for severe mitral stenosis when any symptoms are present if the valve is suitable for percutaneous balloon commissurotomy (may be considered in asymptomatic patients if pulmonary pressure is > 50 mm Hg or there is new-onset atrial fibrillation).

claims.text: Percutaneous balloon commissurotomy is the procedure of choice for younger patients and those without heavily calcified commissures, subvalvular distortion, LA thrombi, or moderate or severe MR
claims.quote: Percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy is the procedure of choice for younger patients and for patients without heavily calcified valve commissures, subvalvular distortion, LA thrombi, or moderate or severe MR (see Table —1).
